prompt: Implement ChannelThresholder.threshold, which pushes each colour channel independently to 0 or 255, and countPure, which counts the pixels that ended up pure white.
explanation: Thresholding each channel separately is not the same as thresholding brightness: a pixel whose red is high but whose blue is low turns into a saturated primary or secondary colour rather than black or white. The shift-and-mask idiom (rgb >> 16) & 0xFF pulls one byte out of the packed int, and (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b puts three bytes back together. Using strictly greater than means a channel exactly equal to the limit falls to 0, which is the edge case the tests check.
hints: Build the output image first, then loop over every (x, y) of the source.
Handle red, green and blue with three separate comparisons -- do not average them.
The comparison is strictly greater than limit, so a channel exactly equal to limit becomes 0.
